question.title: proposal: Change concurrent map writes from fatal to panic
question.caller: A Go runtime map-assignment path and an application/API request handler that has a recovery boundary.
question.input: A map write attempted while the runtime concurrent-write detection condition is true; initial code uses h.flags & hashWriting in mapassign_fast64.
question.output: A catchable panic for the detected concurrent map write, enabling a recovery boundary to contain the failure and respond to the affected request instead of immediately terminating the service.
limits: The author acknowledges correct map access should use a mutex; this request concerns handling a detected misuse, not making unsynchronized maps safe.
The first text does not establish memory safety or map integrity after a race. Such guarantees must not be inferred.
The cited 90% preference is the proposer’s claim, not a measured acceptance criterion.
No behavior is specified for concurrent races the existing detector misses.

whole_must.requirement: At the runtime concurrent-map-write detection branch, signal panic instead of an uncatchable fatal termination.
whole_must.falsifying_input: The hashWriting overlap branch still calls fatal, while only nil-map writes or unrelated application errors panic.
whole_must.predicate: At the runtime concurrent-map-write detection branch, signal panic instead of an uncatchable fatal termination.

whole_must.requirement: Allow a valid recovery boundary to catch that specific concurrent-map-write panic and keep the process available.
whole_must.falsifying_input: A request handler with an applicable recover boundary still loses the whole service when the detector reports concurrent map writes.
whole_must.predicate: Allow a valid recovery boundary to catch that specific concurrent-map-write panic and keep the process available.

whole_must.requirement: Preserve a failing/terminating path for code without a recovery boundary while permitting the recovering API caller to produce an error response such as HTTP 500.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Without recover the invalid write silently succeeds, or with recover the API cannot finish the affected request with an error response.
whole_must.predicate: Preserve a failing/terminating path for code without a recovery boundary while permitting the recovering API caller to produce an error response such as HTTP 500.

partial_must.requirement: Provide the actual map-detector-to-catchable-signal path for detected overlapping writes, rather than a generic panic helper outside the detector.
partial_must.falsifying_input: The component only offers recover() or an exception wrapper; Go’s concurrent-map-write branch still terminates via fatal.
partial_must.predicate: Provide the actual map-detector-to-catchable-signal path for detected overlapping writes, rather than a generic panic helper outside the detector.

partial_must.requirement: Demonstrate that the resulting signal can be caught at an appropriate recovery boundary without mandatory immediate process termination.
partial_must.falsifying_input: The component reports a concurrent-write error by process exit or an uncatchable runtime failure.
partial_must.predicate: Demonstrate that the resulting signal can be caught at an appropriate recovery boundary without mandatory immediate process termination.

question.independent_partial_purpose: Contain the detected map-write failure as a recoverable runtime signal before adding request-specific response handling.
question.independently_useful_next_action: The application recovery boundary can log/translate the caught signal and finish the affected request with an error response.
question.remaining_adapter: Integrate the verified detector behavior into the target Go runtime/version and wire the application recovery boundary to request cleanup/HTTP error reporting. A generic wrapper that leaves fatal unchanged forces the adapter to implement the core action and fails partial completion.
preferences: HTTP 500 is the stated example of request containment, not a requirement for a particular web framework.
No requirement to restore a raced map to a valid state is invented.

named_component_roles.panic/recover: Already explicit mechanism; merely rediscovering generic panic/recover documentation is not a new implementation of the requested map-detector behavior.
named_component_roles.mapassign_fast64: Exact actor shown in the first draft; generic application error wrappers do not replace this runtime branch.

question.same_name_wrong_actor_output_failure: A function named Panic or Recover operating on ordinary returned errors or nil-map writes has the wrong triggering input/actor if concurrent-map-write detection still invokes fatal.

opened.limitation: Does not implement a recoverable map detector; observing guideline is not testing current runtime.
